title: PMA Long Course 159 2026: Eligibility, Age & Selection
metaDescription: PMA Long Course 159 2026 guide: eligibility, age limits, marks, physical standards and the ISSB selection stages for Pakistan Army officer cadets.
headline: PMA Long Course 159: How to Become a Pakistan Army Officer

sections.title: Who can apply for PMA Long Course 159?
sections.content:
PMA Long Course 159 is the Pakistan Army's main route to a Permanent Commission as a Second Lieutenant. It is open to unmarried male citizens of Pakistan, including Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan, who meet the education, age and fitness standards.

Intermediate candidates need at least 60% marks, while two-year graduates need 60% in graduation and 50% at Intermediate. Four-year degree holders also need 60% marks. Serving Army soldiers apply under separate age and marital conditions.

sections.title: Age limits by qualification
sections.content:
Age is counted as on 1 November of the joining year. Intermediate candidates must be 17 to 22 years old, two-year graduates 17 to 23, four-year degree holders 17 to 24, and serving soldiers 17 to 25. A relaxation of up to three months may apply in some categories.

Candidates should check the official advertisement for their exact category before applying, because the limits differ by qualification and a wrong category can end an application early.

sections.title: Selection stages after registration
sections.content:
Applicants register online at joinpakarmy.gov.pk and then face initial written and intelligence tests plus a medical examination at an Army Selection and Recruitment Centre. Successful candidates are called for the four-day ISSB assessment at Kohat, Gujranwala, Malir or Quetta.

The ISSB tests personality, group behaviour, leadership and physical stamina through psychological tests, group tasks and outdoor obstacles. Final selection also includes a medical board and an interview before cadets join PMA Kakul for two years of training.

sections.title: How to prepare well
sections.content:
Good preparation covers English, mathematics, general knowledge and current affairs for the written tests, plus regular running, push-ups and outdoor practice for the physical tasks. Practising group discussion and clear, honest answers helps in the ISSB psychological and interview stages.

Keep original certificates, CNIC or Form B and attested photographs ready, and confirm every date on the official website, because registration windows and test schedules are strictly time-bound.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for PMA Long Course 159?
faqs.a: Intermediate candidates must be 17 to 22 years old, two-year graduates 17 to 23, four-year degree holders 17 to 24, and serving Army soldiers 17 to 25. Age is calculated as on 1 November of the joining year, with up to three months of relaxation possible in some categories.

faqs.q: What marks are needed to apply for PMA 159?
faqs.a: Intermediate candidates need at least 60% marks in FA, FSc, ICS, I.Com, DAE or an equivalent qualification. Two-year graduates need 60% in graduation and 50% at Intermediate, while four-year BS, BA (Hons), BBA or BPA holders need 60% in their degree.

faqs.q: How does selection for PMA Long Course work?
faqs.a: After online registration, candidates take initial written and intelligence tests and a medical examination at an Army Selection and Recruitment Centre. Shortlisted candidates then attend the four-day ISSB assessment, followed by a final medical board, an interview and joining instructions for PMA Kakul.

faqs.q: When did registration for PMA 159 close?
faqs.a: Online registration for PMA Long Course 159 ran from 14 September to 23 October 2026 on joinpakarmy.gov.pk. Candidates who missed this window should prepare now for the next course, which is normally announced about every six months, and verify dates officially.
